spec_match.rationale: Implements the exact CSS Color 4 sRGB transfer pair (c/12.92 below 0.04045, ((c+0.055)/1.055)^2.4 otherwise, and the inverse) that defines what srgb-linear/display-p3-linear mean, and validates it against the browser's real srgb-linear getImageData readback wherever the space exists.

interactive.rationale: A native color input drives the per-channel table live (input event plus a button), and a second control draws the two quantization ramps with a computed distinct-code count.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises encoded/linear/8-bit columns as a labelled computed reference checked against real readback where supported — exactly the page's table and its last column.

edge_cases.rationale: The unsupported branch is honest (the readback column carries the browser's verbatim refusal) and quantization/precision loss is covered by the ramps, but the display-p3-linear variant is described in prose only — the inspector's numeric cross-check runs against srgb-linear alone.

references.rationale: See-also links chromestatus.com/feature/5122501071994880 and the CSS Color 4 srgb-linear definition the math comes from.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's srgb-linear context/ImageData/getImageData readback assertions pin the surface this page cross-checks; the computed columns are explicitly labelled as reference, not as conformance claims.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via CDP: color inspect and ramp draw clicked at 1280×2000 and 360×1600 with zero console errors and post-interaction screenshots read; behind --enable-experimental-web-platform-features the real readback matched the computed reference within ±1 code (e.g. #808080 → 55,55,55 measured), which is the page's match-verdict path.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts inspector-real-matches-computed only when a real readback ran, inspector-computed-only-fallback on the unsupported branch, and ramps-drawn with the measured code counts.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, dark-button/ivory-text pairs with focus-visible rings, table in an overflow scroller, ramps as full-width bordered canvases.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled native color input, scoped table headers, aria-live verdict and ramp outputs that mirror the visual result in numbers, role=img with descriptive labels on both ramp canvases (including what the banding looks like), swatch aria-label updated per color.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 360×1600 DPR3 and 1280×2000: the six-column table scrolls inside its container without widening the page, controls are 44px minimum, ramps scale to container width.

openQuestions.title: Extend the numeric cross-check to display-p3-linear
openQuestions.detail: The same transfer curve applies to P3 primaries, so once display-p3-linear exists in a harness browser the last column could optionally run against a display-p3-linear canvas too (fillStyle in color(display-p3 …) syntax, readback in display-p3-linear) and show that the curve is shared. Prose covers it today; a live column would prove it. In-place additive change to this page.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Visual-only canvas output needs text equivalents and live-region announcements of computed state.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Ramp canvases carry descriptive role=img labels naming the visible effect (smooth vs banding), and the measured distinct-code counts are announced in an aria-live output; the color journey is a real data table, not a picture.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible form controls color picker sliders live region announcements
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use native inputs with visible labels and update results on input with an explicit action alternative.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Native input[type=color] wrapped in a label, updates on input, plus a run button for keyboard/AT users who prefer explicit activation.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Both paths exercised in the CDP run

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Wide tables scroll in their own container; media canvases take width:100% with intrinsic aspect handling.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Six-column table in .scroller{overflow-x:auto}; ramps styled width:100%; at 360×1600 DPR3 the scrollWidth delta is 1px of subpixel rounding on main's own box and horizontal scrolling is impossible (scrollTo(9999,0) leaves scrollX at 0).

summary: Inspection angle: the spec math itself, runnable. Every computed number is labelled computed; the only support claims come from real srgb-linear readbacks, which on flagged Chromium 141 matched the page's implementation of the CSS Color 4 curve within ±1 code value across channels.
